thread:
sara: quick RFC follow-up — I'm leaning toward pushing the fallback decision into a local per-proxy decider instead of relying only on the central arbiter. sketch: locals subscribe to a compacted signal stream, evaluate a small state machine, and flip routes quickly. thoughts?

kevin: fwiw central arbiter gives a clean global view (good for capacity-wide emergencies) but it's a bottleneck for latency-sensitive rollouts. local decider wins on reaction time and partition tolerance, but we need to standardize policies so behaviour is consistent across hosts.

emily: main worry is oscillation / flip-flopping at the edge. how do you prevent two tenants racing their local deciders and thrashing? also need a deterministic audit trail for postmortems.

ravi: proposal: use a sawtooth-style tolerance (not binary). degrade threshold triggers when metric > T for X seconds; recovery requires metric < R for Y seconds where Y > X. add hysteresis and a flip_penalty (token-bucket) so consecutive flips are rate-limited. this prevents quick back-and-forth.

sara: exactly. also: central still exists as a "guidance plane" — it emits global signals and an "override epoch" for emergencies. locals make the final call unless central override with higher epoch is present. advantage: local fastpath + central safety.

kevin: implementation sketch: LocalDecider keeps (policy_id, policy_version, last_flip_ts, score_window). Input: sample stream of probe metrics + central guidance messages. Output: route decision + decision_reason + decision_id for tracing. gRPC streaming of compact diffs (signed) seems easiest. fallback to on-disk event log if stream unavailable.

emily: telemetry needs: per-decision sample_id, feature vector, policy_version, and pre/post latency/cost deltas. these should be attached to traces and emitted as structured logs for ML/eval. remember privacy for tenant ids.

ravi: edge-case: global capacity emergency (e.g., region OOM) — central sets an override with epoch N and instructs locals to immediately move to safe variant. locals must ignore older epochs to avoid replay. add override_fence: {epoch, ttl, signature}.

sara: config example (pseudo):
```
{
  "policy_id": "p-quick-sawtooth",
  "degrade_threshold": 0.95,
  "degrade_window_s": 30,
  "recover_threshold": 0.7,
  "recover_window_s": 120,
  "flip_penalty_s": 10,
  "min_stable_decisions": 5
}
```
this enforces a short degrade window and longer recovery window + penalty.

kevin: lifecycle question — who owns policy tuning? product/desk owns default profiles, eng-runtime owns enforcement/observability, and platform can define tenant overrides. we need a safe rollout path for policy changes (versioned policies + canary-targeted rollout of policy versions).

emily: +1 on versioning. also we should sample decisions for reconstruction: store compact decision events (decision_id, policy_version, inputs_hash, decision). that makes repros fast.

ravi: one more: consider a small consensus check when a local decider tries to flip big traffic (>X%): require acknowledgement from coordinator or from a quorum of neighboring proxies to prevent single-host blast radius. keep default for small flips still local-only.

oncall-bot: noted: added "local-decider" doc item to oncall checklist and created alert template "rapid-flip-detection".

sara: next steps: I'll draft a short RFC with state machine diagram, message contracts (guidance, override, diff stream), and an explainer on sawtooth timelines. tagging kevin/emily/ravi for review. quick poll: prefer a rolling rollout of the policy engine as a dedicated small binary or as a library embedded in the proxy?

kevin: prefer library for faster adoption, but binary gives safer migration boundaries. leaning binary first (canary), then library extraction later.

emily: binary can be canaried independently — +1.

ravi: ok with binary canary then library split. also, include a chaos checklist for partitioned guidance streams.

sara: great — I'll produce RFC draft by end of week. thanks :thumbsup:
